correctness.rationale: The source simplex-volume formula is exactly a Bernstein polynomial of degree \(np\) with coefficients \( inom nj\) followed by zeros. Differentiation gives coefficient differences \( inom n{j+1}- inom nj\), whose nonzero signs change exactly once. After \(x=t/(1-t)\), Descartes' rule permits at most one positive derivative zero, while the constant coefficient is \(n-1>0\) and the last nonzero coefficient is negative, forcing exactly one. The planar quadratic, maximum simplification, and limits are exact consequences. The bundled checker replayed with VERIFY_OK and is explicitly auxiliary.

value.rationale: The imbalance parameter is intrinsic to the newly introduced higher-order body, so its worst value is a natural invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The theorem resolves the entire parameter axis of the simplex benchmark for all dimensions and orders, converts the source's pointwise low-dimensional comparison into a sharp uniform extremal inequality, and yields an explicit planar optimizer and nontrivial large-order constant. This is structurally reusable in any attempt to prove or test the higher-dimensional pointwise conjecture.
